study_identification_part.si_4_title: Personalizing progressive changes to brain structure in Alzheimer's disease using normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The reference (training) dataset was assembled from multiple publicly available sources including OASIS, ABCD, and UK Biobank, totaling 58,836 individuals from 82 sites (described in Rutherford et al. 2022). The research dataset was ADNI (ADNI-1, -GO, -2, -3) with 1,849 participants and 4,540 scans from 62 sites. Because the reference dataset comprises many named datasets (OASIS, ABCD, UK Biobank, and others), it is classified as MULTI-DATASET (UNSPECIFIED OR N>=10).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "a reference (training) dataset comprised of healthy people across the human lifespan ... combining T1-weighted MRI scan data on healthy people from multiple publicly available sources, including Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS), Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study, and UK Biobank (UKB), totaling 58,836 individuals from 82 sites." ... "The research data used in the preparation of this article were obtained from ADNI ... from ADNI-1, -GO, -2, and -3 (n = 1849, a total of 4540 scans)."

answer.ADNI: adaptation/calibration of normative model (70% of cognitively unimpaired controls per ADNI site) and research/test dataset (remaining 30% of controls + MCI + AD participants; n=1181, 3233 scans)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The reference dataset (multiple publicly available sources) was used to train normative models per brain region. The ADNI dataset served dual purposes: 70% of cognitively unimpaired controls (n=666, 1164 scans) were used for transfer learning adaptation/calibration to reduce site and software version effects; the remaining 30% of controls plus all MCI and AD participants (n=1183, 3376 scans before exclusion; final n=1181, 3233 scans) constituted the research dataset for z-score analysis.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "This model was trained on 58,836 scans from datasets across 82 sites to generate normative models per region using the covariates age, sex, and site" ... "The distribution parameters of the reference normative model were calibrated to our ADNI dataset using 70% of cognitively unimpaired controls per ADNI site" ... "The data from the remaining 30% of cognitively unimpaired controls, plus participants with MCI and patients with AD, were then compared to these normative models, generating z scores per region for each scan."

model-1.model-name: neuroanatomical normative model (cortical thickness and subcortical volume)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: One normative model was built for both cortical thickness (148 regions) and subcortical volume (20 regions). The training (reference) dataset comprised 58,836 healthy individuals from 82 sites. For adaptation/calibration to ADNI, 666 cognitively unimpaired ADNI controls (70% of ADNI controls) were used. Overall-phase HC count is 58,836 (reference training) + 666 (adaptation) = 59,502. The remaining 291 ADNI controls were reserved for analysis (not part of normative model building).

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The age demographics of the reference (training) dataset (58,836 individuals) are not reported in this paper. The paper states these were 'healthy people across the human lifespan' and refers to Rutherford et al. (2022) for demographics. For ADNI controls used in analysis (not model building): baseline age mean 73.9, SD 6.2, range 56-93. For the adaptation set (666 ADNI controls), separate age statistics are not reported.
